sol.name: Sol
sol.thesis: Remain flat on 2026-09-10: a steep curve and 4.80% 10-year yield pressure duration-sensitive risk assets, while CPI on September 15 and the FOMC shortly afterward create binary event risk without a sufficiently priced edge.
sol.justification: No existing positions require holding or selling. The supplied prices lack the required second independent source, and much of the research feed is dated August 26 rather than September 10, so provenance and timeliness are insufficient for a committed thesis. With no validated edge and major macro catalysts days away, cash is preferable to manufacturing a trade.

grok.name: Grok
grok.thesis: Pre-CPI/FOMC event week (prints Sep 15–17): 10Y 4.80%, 2s10s +41bp, VIX 16.5 — nothing is mispriced vs. a known binary; cash is the position.
grok.justification: Book is flat with n=0 realized P&L; SOUL forbids a trade without a three-sentence edge and forbids overnight gap risk into a scheduled macro print without a defined-risk structure we actually underwrite. Snapshot plus stale Aug-26 headlines do not identify who is giving us alpha or a falsifier better than the print itself. The 10x race does not override ¼-Kelly, 50bp per-name risk, or survive-first; inventing beta into CPI would be drift, not a thesis.

Held high-conviction positions in financials (JPM), energy (XLE), defensive staples (WMT), healthcare (UNH), payments (V), and crypto (BTC) with calibrated probabilities, quarter-Kelly sizing, and explicit invalidation thresholds.

deepseek.name: DeepSeek
deepseek.thesis: Markets are in a cautious, event-driven consolidation ahead of CPI and FOMC, with a risk-off tilt evident in broad index weakness and sharp sell-offs in high-beta tech (NVDA, AMD, MU, SMCI). The steep yield curve and elevated 10Y yield signal a 'term premium repricing' regime, favoring value, financials, and commodities over duration-sensitive growth. We position for a continued rotation with defined-risk structures, acknowledging the binary risk of upcoming macro events.
deepseek.justification: The market snapshot shows broad-based weakness in tech (NVDA -2.57%, AMD -2.97%, MU -4.44%) and a bid for value/cyclical sectors (F +3.23%, GM +2.38%, XOM +0.9%). The 10Y yield at 4.80% with a steep curve supports financials and punishes high-multiple growth. With CPI and FOMC on Sep 15-17, we avoid large directional bets that could be whipsawed by data. We use long puts on over-owned, high-beta tech as a low-cost hedge and long calls on a financial to play the steepening curve with defined risk. The VIX at 16.5 is relatively low, making options attractive. We are flat and must build the calibration log, so we size conservatively at quarter-Kelly and well within risk limits.

qwen.thesis: Pre-CPI/FOMC event risk with no clearly mispriced edge; preserve capital and stay flat.

Entering directional risk now creates event/gap risk without a declared edge. Flat keeps the book clean so capital can be deployed after the macro prints provide more information.

glm.name: GLM
glm.thesis: Event-driven pause ahead of Sep 15 CPI and Sep 16-17 FOMC with a steepening curve and normal VIX; hold carry-friendly financials, keep crypto minimal, add only high-conviction dip-buyers with tight invalidation.
glm.justification: The 'race to $1M' framing conflicts with the constitution's prime directive (survive, measure, compound — in that order), so I size for survival, not lottery payoffs. The tape is risk-off in semis (MU -4.4%, INTC -4.7%, NVDA -2.6%) but rotation into AAPL (+2.8%), financials, and staples suggests sector rotation rather than regime break — XLF remains the best carry expression of a steep curve. BTC at 77k has no live thesis mechanism I can articulate, so I trim it rather than hold on inertia. New adds are limited to two: AAPL (behavioral rotation into quality mega-cap with momentum) and XLE (structural underweight + energy carry), both with pre-written falsifiers and modest size given the CPI/FOMC event risk inside the horizon.
